source: If you listened to this station non-stop from midnight to 11:59pm today, you’d likely only hear 3 back-to-back songs by women, compared to 245 from men.
claim: On KCYY-FM's 1/7/22 log, 3 songs are back-to-back women's plays and 245 are back-to-back men's plays.

source: We looked at 19 dates throughout 2022 for this same radio station and found that out of 6,474 songs, only 64 (0.99%) were back-to-back songs by women plays. For back-to-back songs by men, it was 4,231 (65.53%). Back-to-back mixed-gender ensembles and collaborations account for 36 (0.56%) songs.
claim: Of KCYY-FM's 6,474 songs, 64 (0.99%) are back-to-back women's plays, 4,231 (65.35%) are back-to-back men's plays, and 36 (0.56%) are mixed-gender back-to-backs.
code: d[d.gender.notna()].assign(b=lambda x: np.where(x.gender.eq(x.groupby(['station','date'])['gender'].shift()), x.gender, 'not')).query("station=='KCYY-FM'").groupby(['station','b']).size().to_frame('n').assign(pct=lambda y: y.n/y.n.sum()*100, total=lambda y: y.n.sum())

source: For this station on average, 4 back-to-back women’s songs are played on release days compared to 3 songs on “regular” Fridays.
claim: KCYY-FM averages 4.14 back-to-back women's plays on release dates versus 2.92 on regular Fridays.
code: d[d.gender.notna()].assign(b=lambda x: np.where(x.gender.eq(x.groupby(['station','date'])['gender'].shift()), x.gender, 'not')).query("station=='KCYY-FM'").assign(rel=lambda x: np.where(x.weekday.str.contains('regular'),'regular Fridays','release dates')).groupby(['station','rel','date']).b.agg(lambda s: s.eq('women').sum()).groupby(['station','rel']).mean()

source: When you recode mixed-gender collaborations and mixed-gender ensembles as songs by women artists, as some radio stations do, you get 200 (3.1%) women’s back-to-back plays, roughly 10 per day for this station.
claim: Recoding mixed-gender songs as women's gives KCYY-FM 200 back-to-back women's plays, 3.09% of its songs and 10.53 per day.
code: d[(d.gender.notna())&(d.station=='KCYY-FM')].assign(g2=lambda x: x.gender.replace('male-female','women')).assign(w2=lambda x: x.g2.eq('women') & x.g2.eq(x.groupby(['station','date'])['g2'].shift())).groupby('station').agg(n=('w2','sum'), pct=('w2', lambda s: s.mean()*100), days=('date','nunique')).assign(per_day=lambda y: y.n/y.days)

source: Percentage of back-to-back women plays by station
claim: Back-to-back women's plays as a share of each station's songs run from 0.03% at Cincinnati's WUBE-FM to 1.27% at Los Angeles's KKGO-FM, with San Antonio's KCYY-FM third at 0.99%.

source: For some of the stations, you could go a full day or more without hearing a song by women played back-to-back.
claim: 166 of the 551 station-days have no back-to-back women's play, and Cincinnati's WUBE-FM has 17 such days out of 19.
code: d[d.gender.notna()].assign(b=lambda x: np.where(x.gender.eq(x.groupby(['station','date'])['gender'].shift()), x.gender, 'not')).groupby(['city','station','date']).b.agg(lambda s: s.eq('women').sum()).to_frame('n').assign(is_zero=lambda y: y.n.eq(0)).groupby(['city','station']).agg(days=('is_zero','size'), zero_days=('is_zero','sum')).assign(all_days=lambda y: y.days.sum(), all_zero=lambda y: y.zero_days.sum()).sort_values('zero_days', ascending=False)

source: Percentage of back-to-back spins for songs by women by time of day
claim: Averaged across stations, 46.1% of women's back-to-back plays are overnight (OVN), 16.6% in morning drive (AMD), 9.7% midday (MID), 8.5% in afternoon drive (PMD) and 19.0% in the evening (EVE).

source: On average, 65.1% percent of songs by women played back-to-back come during these hours

source: Where back-to-back spins for songs by women were on average 0.5% of all airplay, back-to-back spins for songs by all artists of color averaged 0.38% and back-to-back spins for those by women artists of color were non-existent.
claim: Averaged across stations, back-to-back women's plays are 0.50% of songs, back-to-back plays by artists of color (a song by an artist of color following a same-gender song by an artist of color) are 0.38%, and women artists of color have none.

source: It’ll be 9 hours and 16 minutes before you hear a rarity on country radio: back-to-back songs by women with Priscilla Block’s “Just About Over You” played right after the Carly Pearce and Ashley McBryde’s collaboration “Never Wanted To Be That Girl.”
claim: On KCYY-FM's 1/7/22 log, the first women's back-to-back after the 8:35 a.m. song comes 9 hours 16 minutes later, at 5:51 p.m., when Priscilla Block's 'Just About Over You' follows Carly Pearce and Ashley McBryde's 'Never Wanted To Be That Girl'.
